summary: Read the abstract of Tseng (Math. Z. 302 (2022), arXiv:2106.00836, verified via arXiv API): a closed horocycle of length ℓ equidistributes on the cusp neighbourhood shrinking at rate T^{−1} whenever T/ℓ→0 (segment condition max{T^{−1/6},(T/ℓ)^{1/2}}(T/ℓ)^{−δ}, which is trivial for the full closed horocycle). So the deepest reachable target for a closed horocycle of length p has measure ≈1/T with T=p^{1−o(1)}, i.e. measure p^{−1+o(1)}, and the expected number of visits is ℓ/T=p^{o(1)}. Kelmer (arXiv:1708.08953) treats logarithm laws/shrinking targets for discrete flows and does not give the closed-horocycle depth.

summary: Wrote the (★) count as a sum over levels: R(p)=Σ_C #{d | 4Cp+1: d≡−1 (mod 4C)}, a divisor function in the progression −1 mod 4C with modulus q=4C and length N=4Cp+1. summary: Exact orthogonality identity: for gcd(N,m)=1, Σ_{χ mod m} χ̄(−1)χ(d) = φ(m)·[d≡−1 (mod m)], so Σ_{χ≠1} χ̄(−1)σ_χ(N) = φ(m)·D⁻_m(N) − τ(N). Hence at any level with no certificate (D⁻=0) the nontrivial twisted sum equals −τ(N) exactly (ratio 1), and in general |Σ_{χ≠1}|/τ(N)=|φ(m)D⁻/τ(N) − 1|. The item's 'how close it gets' is therefore determined by D⁻: it is never small when D⁻=0. (Derived by orthogonality; not brute-force verified over characters.)
